why: A weak, non-essential kinase: trust the engine and the generic recalls; the co-essential link (r 0.27) is too weak.
Barely expressed (2.8 nTPM); the engine plus generic K562 responses; an RPE1 PTEN record says nothing about MOK.
A haematopoietic transcription factor expressed in K562; LMO2 (same blood-programme family) adds a little.
A cilia dynein-2 light chain, likely mild in K562; the essential DYNLL1/2 partners overstate it.
Complex I subunit: NDUFS5 (same complex, r 0.79) is the best guide; RAN and 14-3-3 recalls are unrelated.
SMC5/6 complex: NSMCE1 and SMC6 knockdowns are the same machine; RAN and YWHAE are unrelated.
Weak, non-essential; the co-essential link is negligible.
Endocytic GEF: SH3GL1 (endocytosis) and its partner YWHAE help a little; CK1-alpha loss is far stronger than GAPVD1's.
A non-essential glycosyltransferase; keep the engine and generic responses.
Mitoribosome small subunit: MRPS14 (same subunit, r 0.62) and its own RPE1 knockdown; cytosolic ribosome partners and spliceosome recalls are the wrong machine.
A weakly expressed cancer-testis antigen: its partner SUPT5H is an essential elongation factor whose loss is far stronger, and its RPE1 record is noise.
Mitotic kinase: MAD2L1 (spindle checkpoint) and AURKB's own RPE1 knockdown are the closest guides; RAN, SNRPD3 and PTGES3 are unrelated.
A neuropeptide barely expressed in K562; no specific effect expected.
YBEY matures the mitochondrial small-subunit rRNA; FOXRED1 (respiratory chain, r 0.61) shares the mitochondrial programme, the 14-3-3 recalls do not.
TGFBRAP1 is the CORVET VPS3 subunit acting with RAB5: VPS16 (shared core) and RAB5C (r 0.35) both raised cholesterol synthesis.
Barely expressed (1.4 nTPM); no specific effect expected.
aPKC is not needed for K562 growth; HNF1B is not expressed in K562, so its co-essential link is meaningless here.
A redundant Holliday-junction resolvase; little effect expected; RMI1 (r 0.22) is a weak link.
A low-expressed KRAB zinc finger; TRIM28 loss affects hundreds of such factors at once and overstates it.
Essential recombinase: RAD51C (same HR step) is the best guide; RPE1 adds a p53 response that p53-null K562 lacks, so it counts less.
Uncharacterised and weakly expressed; FOXH1 (r 0.23) is not expressed in K562.
A non-essential Rab; the GDI2 partner hints at trafficking (cholesterol), but GDIs serve all Rabs, so only a little weight.
Proteasome ATPase: PSMD2, PSMC4 and PSMC1 knockdowns are the same machine, giving the proteasome bounce-back and ribosomal mRNA fall; RAN and YWHAE are unrelated.
PAN2-PAN3 deadenylase: PAN2 is the same complex; PABPC1 loss is far broader.
A mitochondrial transport adaptor with little growth role; the OGT and DYNLL2 partners act far more broadly.
A surface adhesion protein; no specific source, keep the engine.
GAK uncoats clathrin vesicles: CLTC loss (r 0.31) raised cholesterol synthesis (blocked LDL uptake), which the engine also predicts.
Non-essential; no informative partner or co-essential record.
Weakly expressed; keep the engine and generic K562 responses.
A minor tubulin isoform covered by TUBA1A/1B; chaperonin (CCT) loss is far stronger and unrelated in effect.
ASCC3 works with ASCC2 in ribosome quality control and repair, so ASCC2's knockdown is the best guide.
A large-subunit ribosomal protein: RPL6 gives the ribosomal-loss signature; RPL36AL may soften it, so keep the engine too.
A modest mitotic/adhesion protein; BYSL and USP5 losses are far stronger and unrelated.
The 3M-complex cullin; SF3B3 and SKP1 are broad essential partners; its own RPE1 knockdown matches the engine.
ARF4 covers for ARF5; BUB1 (r 0.17) is a chance link.
A chromatin protein with a modest K562 role; the co-essential link (r 0.19) is weak.
A non-essential mitochondrial nucleotide kinase; keep the engine.
60S ribosome biogenesis: PWP1 (r 0.31, same process) and the ribosomal-protein recalls (RPL15, RPSA) carry the ribosome-loss signature.
Not expressed in K562 (1.9 nTPM); its ELMO2 co-essentiality comes from adherent cells.
Mitoribosome large subunit: MRPL37, MRPL10 and MRPL15 share the MT-ND-up signature, as does its own RPE1 knockdown.
An ERAD adaptor: UBE2G2 (ERAD E2, r 0.46) and its own RPE1 knockdown both raise ER chaperones (HSPA5, SDF2L1, CALR); VCP is broader.
LSM12 binds ATXN2L directly, so it is the best partner guide; DDX6 is a broader P-body helicase.
A lysosomal lipid phosphatase with a mild role; LAMTOR1 and BLOC1S2 hint at lysosome and lipid genes but act more strongly.
